stages.a: A ripened block stands upright. A razor slice opens across the top.
stages.v: Ripen 1-2 weeks or more past full colonization, until caramel droplets form and a rust ring shows in the headspace. Then stand it upright, slice 3-6 mm deep across the top and press the air out.

stages.a: Small knots bead along the cut. Most stay small; a few become mushrooms.
stages.v: Hyphal knots appear along the cut first. Recognisable baby mushrooms follow in about 7-10 days.

stages.a: Tight round buttons on fused stems. Every cap is scaly and still sealed to its stem.
stages.v: Fruit cold and foggy: pin at 10 to about 16 °C (ideal 13-16 °C), 90-95% RH, CO2 below about 900 ppm.

stages.a: The caps widen and pull away from the stems. The veil under each cap stretches thin.
stages.v: After primordia, about 16-17 °C and 88-90% RH. The slowest of the mixed species: 7-12 more days from babies to harvest.

stages.a: The veil tears at the cap edge and the gills show, still half covered. The caps are still rounded.
stages.v: Pick while the gills are still semi-covered and before the caps flatten. One day late sharply cuts shelf life. Clusters do not mature in sync.

stages.a: The caps flatten and tip, the gills open wide and the stems sag.
stages.v: Picked late, it keeps badly. If the room is too warm, caps flatten fast, stems wither, and the mushrooms droop and smell bad.

labels.a: A rust-coloured band on the bag wall, just above the block.
labels.v: A rust-coloured ring in the headspace is one sign the block is ripe.

labels.a: Caramel-coloured droplets beading on the block top.
labels.v: A ripening block swells with caramel-coloured metabolites and turns golden-mustard, which new staff mistake for Neurospora.

labels.a: The slice across the top of the block.
labels.v: A cross, an X, or a razor slice about 3-6 mm deep across the top. Chestnut takes a slightly deeper cut than most. No half-moons around pins already there.

labels.a: White knots along the cut: the very first sign of mushrooms.
labels.v: Knots first, then baby mushrooms in about 7-10 days.

labels.a: Slender stems, fused low down where the cluster leaves the cut.
Raised scales over the cap, thickest at the centre.
labels.v: Speckled, scaly caps: it photographs very well, which helps at market and online.

labels.a: The partial veil: a skin from the cap edge to the stem that covers the gills.
labels.v: The gills should still be semi-covered when you pick.

labels.a: The cap edge, still rolled in toward the stem.
The veil splits at the cap edge: the cap is separating from the stem.
labels.v: This is the picking point: gills still semi-covered, caps not yet flat.

labels.a: Gills under the cap, showing through the torn veil.
labels.v: Harvest while the gills are still semi-covered. One day late sharply cuts storage life.

labels.a: A younger mushroom in the same cluster, still a button.
labels.v: Clusters do not mature in sync. Trade some yield for shelf life.

labels.a: The cap opens out flat and its edge lifts.
labels.v: Too warm a room: caps flatten fast, stems wither, and the mushrooms droop and smell bad.

labels.a: What is left of the veil hangs on the stem as a ragged ring.
